experiences.name: Meia Praia Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxed afternoon at Meia Praia, one of the longest and most accessible beaches in the Algarve, located just minutes from Lagos town center. Ideal for a late Day 1 arrival — simply drop bags at a Lagos-based hotel and walk to the beach. Calm waters, golden sand, and beachside bars make it perfect for unwinding after a long flight without needing transport.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Cliff Walk and Swim
experiences.description: Explore the iconic golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear coves of Praia da Marinha, consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Stay in Carvoeiro or Lagoa to be within 10 minutes of this spot, avoiding long transfers. Morning visits offer calmer waters and fewer crowds, perfect for snorkeling and cliff photography.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine and Seafood Pairing Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided wine tasting session at a local quinta near Lagoa, the heart of Algarve wine country, sampling regional Negra Mole and Arinto wines paired with fresh local seafood and cheeses. Sessions typically run 2–3 hours and are hosted mid-morning, making them ideal for Day 2 or 3 when you are fully settled. Book a hotel in Lagoa or Silves to be within 15 minutes of multiple quintas.

experiences.name: Silves Castle and Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Discover the Moorish Silves Castle and wander the cobblestone streets of Portugal's former Algarve capital. Combine culture with food by joining a guided walking tour that stops at local taverns for regional wines, cataplana seafood stew, and medronho brandy. Silves is centrally located and easily reachable from Lagoa or Carvoeiro hotels in under 20 minutes, keeping transfers short and maximizing your day.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the famous Benagil Cave, one of the Algarve's most spectacular natural wonders, on a guided kayak tour departing directly from Benagil Beach. Tours last approximately 2 hours and depart in the morning when seas are calmest. Stay in Carvoeiro, just 5 km away, to avoid long travel and ensure you catch the early morning slot before afternoon winds pick up. A highlight activity well within budget.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Take the Rede Expressos bus or Eva bus from Faro Airport to Lagos (approx. 1.5-2 hours, ~€6-8). Check in to Boutique Taghostel on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos. Drop off luggage and freshen up.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a nearby 24h convenience store or a kebab/pizza slice shop near the hostel in central Lagos (~€3-5)

day_by_day.notes: Keep some euros handy for the bus. The Taghostel is centrally located in Lagos, making it easy to walk everywhere. Confirm check-in arrangements with the hostel in advance for late arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After waking, take a leisurely walk to explore central Lagos. Visit the historic Praça Gil Eanes (main square) and the Igreja de Santo António (small entry fee ~€2). Stroll along the old town walls and enjoy the charming cobblestone streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 15 minutes to the iconic Ponta da Piedade — dramatic golden limestone cliffs and sea caves. Explore the viewpoints for free. Optionally rent a kayak or join a shared boat tour to see the caves up close (~€15-20 for budget group tours departing from Lagos marina).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Meia Praia beach (accessible by free ferry from Lagos marina, ~€1 each way) for a sunset stroll. Return to town and explore the lively Rua 25 de Abril bar street.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha or a local pastelaria near the hostel — coffee + pastel de nata (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Grab a prego (steak sandwich) or bifana at a local tasca near the market (~€4-6)
meals.dinner: O Camilo or a local restaurant near the marina — grilled sardines or peixe do dia (fish of the day) with bread and salad (~€10-14)

day_by_day.notes: September weather in the Algarve is typically warm and sunny (24-28°C), perfect for beaches. Sunscreen and water are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short walk or taxi (~€5) to Praia Dona Ana, one of Lagos's most beautiful beaches. Arrive early to claim a good spot. Swim and relax on the golden sands surrounded by dramatic rock formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the cliff path from Praia Dona Ana toward Praia do Camilo (15-minute walk). Descend the wooden staircase to this secluded gem of a beach. Continue exploring the coastal path toward Ponta da Piedade viewpoints.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos town center. Visit the Mercado de Lagos (farmers market area) for fresh local produce. Enjoy a relaxed evening in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast if available, or a local café — toast, juice, and coffee (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the local supermarket (Pingo Doce or Lidl near the center) — bread, cheese, local ham, fruit (~€5-6)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina near the marina — hearty Portuguese cataplana or grilled fish (~€10-13)

day_by_day.notes: Praia do Camilo has a small entry fee for the staircase (~€1.50). Bring cash. The cliff walk is free and offers stunning views.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres (30 km west of Lagos). Take the Eva bus from Lagos bus station (~€4.50 each way, ~45 min). Visit the impressive Fortaleza de Sagres (fortress at the southwestern tip of Europe, entry ~€3). Walk the dramatic clifftop paths.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Praia do Beliche or Praia de Mareta in Sagres — wild, windswept Atlantic beaches with powerful waves. Great for surfing or just watching surfers. Explore the village of Sagres.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus. Relax at the hostel or explore the evening atmosphere in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Quick coffee and pastry at Lagos bus station café (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: A Tasca in Sagres village — fresh tuna steak or grilled fish, very popular with locals (~€9-12)
meals.dinner: Nah Nah Bah burger bar in Lagos — great burgers and craft beer, popular with budget travelers (~€8-11)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is windier and cooler than Lagos — bring a light jacket. The last bus back to Lagos is usually around 19:00-20:00, so check the schedule at the bus station.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Take the Eva bus or a rideshare to Portimão (20 km east, ~€3.50 by bus). Visit the Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (book in advance, budget tour ~€15-20 including tasting of 3-4 wines). The winery is known for its Algarve reds and whites.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the winery, head to Praia da Rocha in Portimão — one of the Algarve's most famous beaches with a long golden stretch of sand. Swim and relax. Explore the clifftop promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Portimão town center. Visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sundays, otherwise ~€3) if time allows. Return to Lagos by bus.

meals.breakfast: Hostel or local café in Lagos before departure (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Light snack at the winery or a café in Estômbar (~€5-7)
meals.dinner: Tasca da Dona Barca in Portimão or a local restaurant near Praia da Rocha — grilled chicken or pork with potatoes (~€9-12) before heading back

day_by_day.notes: Book the winery tour at least 2-3 days in advance. Quinta dos Vales offers some of the most affordable winery experiences in the Algarve. Uber/Bolt may be cheaper than bus for the winery leg.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Lagos's local market — Mercado Municipal de Lagos (open mornings, free entry). Browse fresh fish, vegetables, local cheeses, and honey. Great for picking up budget snacks and local products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle from a local shop near the hostel (~€10-12/day) and cycle to Meia Praia — a long, quieter beach 3 km east of Lagos. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing on this less-crowded stretch of sand.
day_by_day.evening: Cycle back to Lagos. Enjoy a sunset drink at one of the rooftop bars or cliff-edge bars near the marina. Try a local Medronho (arbutus berry spirit) or a glass of Algarve wine.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit and pastries from the market (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Meia Praia — toasted sandwich or salad (~€6-8)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Vivant or a local tasca in Lagos old town — pork alentejana (pork with clams) or bacalhau (~€10-13)

day_by_day.notes: Bicycle rental shops are plentiful near the hostel. Meia Praia is ideal for a quieter beach day compared to the more touristy spots. The ferry to Meia Praia costs ~€1 if you prefer not to cycle.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — the historic Moorish capital of the Algarve (30 km northeast of Lagos). Take the train from Lagos station (~€3.50, 40 min to Tunes, then change, or bus ~€4). Visit the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves (entry ~€2.80) with panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves old town — the Gothic Cathedral (free entry), the Roman bridge, and the charming riverside. Walk along the Arade River. Visit the local market if it's running. Silves is also surrounded by orange and almond groves.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a quiet evening at the hostel or join fellow travelers for drinks in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and toast at Lagos train station café (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves — popular budget-friendly café near the castle with great views (~€8-10)
meals.dinner: O Cantinho do Zé or a local tasca in Lagos — daily special (prato do dia) which is the most budget-friendly option (~€7-9 including drink)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a fantastic off-the-beaten-path destination. The castle is one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal. Check train/bus schedules in advance as connections can be infrequent.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Porto de Mós — a beautiful, less-crowded beach about 2 km south of Lagos center (20-minute walk or short taxi). Enjoy the morning calm before the crowds arrive. The beach is backed by cliffs and has clear turquoise water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the coastal cliff path from Porto de Mós toward Praia da Luz (about 5 km west, 1.5-hour scenic walk). Arrive at the charming village of Luz with its white-washed houses and calm bay beach. Swim and relax.
day_by_day.evening: Take a local bus back to Lagos from Luz (~€2). Enjoy the evening in Lagos — browse the artisan shops and souvenir stalls in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local café (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Praia de Porto de Mós or pack a picnic (~€5-7)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Fortaleza da Luz in Praia da Luz (before heading back) or a Lagos restaurant — fresh grilled fish (~€10-13)

day_by_day.notes: The cliff walk between Porto de Mós and Luz is one of the most scenic coastal walks in the western Algarve. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water. The path can be uneven in places.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting experience! Take a bus or Bolt to Herdade dos Pimenteiros or Quinta da Penina near Portimão/Alvor area. Alternatively, visit Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's winery) near Guia — book a tour in advance (~€15-20 for tasting). These offer insight into Algarve wine production.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the winery, head to Praia de Alvor (near Portimão) — a stunning beach with a beautiful estuary and boardwalk through the dunes. Walk the nature boardwalk through the Alvor estuary (free) — great for birdwatching.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming fishing village of Alvor — narrow cobblestone streets, whitewashed houses, and a lively waterfront. Return to Lagos by bus.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hostel or a café before departure (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Winery lunch or a café in Alvor village — fresh seafood petiscos (tapas) (~€8-10)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celso in Alvor or back in Lagos — grilled sea bass or dorada (~€10-13)

day_by_day.notes: The Alvor estuary boardwalk is a hidden gem and completely free. September is still warm enough for swimming at Alvor beach. Book winery tours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Lazy beach morning at Praia de Lagos (the main town beach, walking distance from the hostel). Rent a paddleboard or bodyboard (~€10-15/hour) for some water sports fun. The September sea is warm and calm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos) in Lagos — the only one of its kind in Europe (entry ~€3). Learn about Lagos's significant and sobering role in the Age of Exploration. Then visit the nearby Igreja de Santa Maria.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free walking tour of Lagos old town (tip-based, ~€5-10 tip recommended). These usually depart from Praça Gil Eanes in the late afternoon/early evening. Great way to learn the city's history.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mota near the hostel — coffee, fresh orange juice, and croissant (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Supermarket picnic on the beach — Pingo Doce has great ready-made meals (~€4-6)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Casinha do Petisco in Lagos — traditional Portuguese petiscos (small plates) to share, great value (~€10-12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Slave Market Museum is small but historically significant and very affordable. Free walking tours are a great budget way to get local insights — search for Lagos Free Walking Tour online.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Carrapateira and Praia da Bordeira (50 km north of Lagos, in the Costa Vicentina Natural Park). Rent a car for the day (~€25-35 from a local budget agency) or join a shared tour. Praia da Bordeira is a wild, vast Atlantic beach — one of the most spectacular in Portugal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Praia do Amado — a world-class surf beach nearby. Watch surfers or take a beginner surf lesson (~€25-30 for a 2-hour group lesson). Explore the dramatic dune landscape of the Natural Park.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Lagos via the scenic EN120 road through the Algarve hinterland. Return the rental car.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hostel before picking up the car (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Tasca do Prego in Carrapateira village — simple, delicious local food, very popular with surfers (~€8-10)
meals.dinner: Back in Lagos — Restaurante O Galeão or similar — grilled chicken piri-piri with fries (~€9-11)

day_by_day.notes: Car rental is the most practical option for this day trip. Book in advance for the best rates. The Costa Vicentina is a protected natural park with some of Europe's most unspoiled beaches. Fuel costs approximately €10-15 for the round trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — revisit your favorite beach or try Praia do Camilo one more time. Take your time and soak up the last of the Algarve sun. Swim, read, and relax.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for some last-minute souvenir shopping in the old town. Pick up local products: Algarve wine, local honey, almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos), dried figs, or handmade ceramics. Visit the local artisan shops on Rua 25 de Abril.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Lagos. Splurge slightly on a nicer meal to celebrate the trip. Enjoy a final sunset walk along the marina and the old town walls.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or favorite local café (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach snack bar (~€6-8)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina or Dom Sebastião — treat yourself to a proper Portuguese seafood dinner: cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) (~€15-20 as a slight splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Dom Rodrigos (almond and egg sweets) are the iconic Algarve sweet — available in most pastry shops and make great gifts. Budget souvenir shops are plentiful in the old town.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Boutique Taghostel (store luggage if needed). Take a final morning stroll through Lagos old town — visit the Praça da República and the waterfront one last time. Grab a final pastel de nata and coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Faro Airport for departure. Take the Eva/Rede Expressos bus from Lagos bus station to Faro Airport (~€6-8, 1.5-2 hours). Arrive at the airport with plenty of time before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. End of the Algarve adventure!

meals.breakfast: Final coffee and pastry at a Lagos café — savor the last pastel de nata (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Snack at Lagos bus station or Faro Airport — sandwich or light meal (~€5-8)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight

day_by_day.notes: The Lagos to Faro Airport bus runs several times daily. Check the current schedule at the Lagos bus station or online (eva-bus.com). Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for the bus journey plus airport check-in. Total estimated budget for 13 days (excluding flights): accommodation ~€15-25/night at hostel, food ~€20-30/day, activities ~€5-15/day, transport ~€5-10/day = approximately €500-700 total.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the airport shuttle or a pre-booked taxi (~1 hour) to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your room.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a nearby 24-hour café or convenience store near the hostel on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, or order delivery if available.

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives late — keep Day 1 completely free of planned activities. Confirm taxi or transfer in advance. Boutique Taghostel is centrally located in Lagos old town, making it easy to walk everywhere from Day 2 onward.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a slow morning walk through Lagos old town — explore the historic Praça Gil Eanes, the Igreja de Santa Maria, and the old city walls. Get oriented with your surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia Beach Day — one of the longest and most accessible beaches in the Algarve, just a short taxi or water taxi ride from Lagos marina. Spend a relaxed afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and unwinding on the wide sandy shore.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos and stroll along the marina at sunset. Enjoy the lively atmosphere of the waterfront before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha or a local pastelaria near the hostel — enjoy a galão (milky coffee) and pastel de nata for a classic Portuguese start.
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Meia Praia — grilled sardines, a fresh salad, and a cold Sagres beer.
meals.dinner: O Camilo Restaurant near Lagos — mid-range seafood with stunning cliff views. Try the grilled sea bass or cataplana de marisco (seafood stew). Budget ~€20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Meia Praia is reachable by a short water taxi from Lagos marina (very affordable) or a 10-minute taxi ride. September weather is typically warm and sunny — perfect beach conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the famous Ponta da Piedade — a dramatic series of golden limestone sea stacks and grottos just south of Lagos. Walk the clifftop trail for panoramic views, then descend the steps to the water's edge. Optionally hire a small boat tour from the base (~€10–15) to explore the sea caves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lagos town itself — visit the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos), the historic Praça da República, and browse the local artisan shops and ceramic stores along Rua 25 de Abril.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening in Lagos old town, popping into wine bars and tapas spots.

meals.breakfast: At the hostel or a nearby café — toast with local queijo fresco (fresh cheese) and fruit.
meals.lunch: Tasca do Celso in Lagos old town — a beloved local tasca serving hearty Portuguese lunch specials like bacalhau à brás (codfish with eggs and potatoes). Budget ~€10–15.
meals.dinner: Adega da Marina in Lagos — a rustic mid-range restaurant known for grilled meats and regional wines. Try the piri-piri chicken or grilled tuna. Budget ~€18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Ponta da Piedade is a 20-minute walk south from the hostel or a short taxi ride. Wear comfortable shoes for the clifftop walk. The boat tours at the base are informal and cash-based — bring small bills.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres — take a local bus or rent a car for the day. Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres (Sagres Fortress) perched on the windswept southwestern tip of Europe. Explore the historic wind compass (Rosa dos Ventos) and learn about Portugal's Age of Discovery.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Sagres, visit Praia do Beliche or Praia da Mareta — wild, rugged Atlantic beaches with powerful waves and stunning scenery. These are less crowded than central Algarve beaches and have a raw, dramatic beauty.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by early evening. Relax and freshen up before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hostel or grab a pastel de nata and coffee from a local bakery before catching the bus.
meals.lunch: A Tasca in Sagres village — a simple, authentic local restaurant serving fresh fish of the day and regional soups. Budget ~€12–18.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Mullens in Lagos — a popular mid-range spot with a great selection of Algarve wines and grilled fish. Budget ~€20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Buses run from Lagos to Sagres (Eva Transportes) roughly every 1–2 hours and take about 1 hour. Alternatively, renting a car for the day (~€30–40) gives more flexibility. Sagres can be windy even in September — bring a light layer.

day_by_day.morning: Travel east along the coast to Praia da Marinha Cliff Walk and Swim. Take a bus or taxi to Lagoa/Carvoeiro area (~45 minutes from Lagos). Begin the iconic cliff walk along the golden limestone formations — one of the most photographed coastlines in Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Praia da Marinha itself for a swim in the crystal-clear turquoise coves. The water here is exceptionally clear and the rock formations create natural sheltered pools. Spend the afternoon swimming and exploring the small sea caves accessible from the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Head into the nearby village of Carvoeiro for the evening — a charming small resort town with a pretty beach and good restaurant options.

meals.breakfast: At the hostel or a café in Lagos before departing.
meals.lunch: Picnic on the cliffs — pick up fresh bread, local cheese, cured meats, and fruit from a Lagos supermarket (Pingo Doce or Lidl) before leaving. Budget ~€8–10.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Boneca in Carvoeiro — a well-regarded mid-range restaurant with fresh seafood and Algarve wines. Try the grilled octopus or the catch of the day. Budget ~€20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Marinha is consistently rated one of the best beaches in Europe. The cliff walk is moderately easy but involves some uneven terrain — wear sturdy sandals or trainers. The beach itself has limited facilities, so bring water and snacks. Return to Lagos by bus or taxi in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Algarve Wine and Seafood Pairing Experience — a guided wine tasting session at a local quinta near Lagoa, the heart of Algarve wine country. Learn about the unique terroir of the region, taste indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Arinto, and enjoy expertly paired local seafood bites.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the wine experience, explore the town of Lagoa itself — visit the Igreja Matriz de Lagoa and browse the local market if it's running. Pick up a bottle or two of Algarve wine to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a relaxed evening. Visit a local wine bar to continue the wine theme of the day.

meals.breakfast: At the hostel — a proper sit-down breakfast to prepare for the wine tasting.
meals.lunch: Included as part of the wine and seafood pairing experience at the quinta.
meals.dinner: Vinha Bar in Lagos — a cozy wine bar and restaurant in the old town with an excellent selection of Portuguese wines by the glass and small plates. Budget ~€15–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Algarve Wine and Seafood Pairing Experience in advance as group sizes are limited. Lagoa is about 30–40 minutes from Lagos by bus or taxi. The experience typically lasts 2–3 hours. Designated driver or taxi recommended for the return trip after wine tasting.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and leisure morning in Lagos. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and take a gentle walk along the Lagos seafront promenade (Avenida dos Descobrimentos) and down to Praia dos Estudantes or Praia da Batata — small, sheltered town beaches perfect for a casual morning swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a kayak or stand-up paddleboard from Lagos marina (~€15–20 for 2 hours) and paddle along the coastline toward Ponta da Piedade, exploring sea caves and arches from the water.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a slightly more upscale dinner to mark the halfway point of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mira Mar near the hostel — a local favourite for fresh pastries, toast, and coffee. Budget ~€5–7.
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Praia da Batata — light lunch of a bifana (pork sandwich) or tosta mista and a cold drink. Budget ~€8–10.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dom Sebastião in Lagos — one of the most respected restaurants in town, known for traditional Algarvian cuisine and an excellent wine list. Try the cataplana or the grilled monkfish. Budget ~€28–38 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Kayak and paddleboard rentals are available from several operators along Lagos marina — no booking required, just show up. The sea cave kayaking route is best done in calm morning or afternoon conditions. September seas are generally calm.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — take the train from Lagos to Silves (about 40 minutes, very scenic). Begin with the Silves Castle and Old Town Food Walk — explore the impressive red sandstone Moorish castle, one of the best-preserved in Portugal, with panoramic views over the orange groves and hills.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the food walk through Silves old town — wander the cobblestone streets, visit the Gothic Sé Catedral de Silves, browse the local ceramic shops, and stop at traditional tascas for regional bites. Try medronho (local arbutus berry spirit) at a local bar.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by train or bus. Enjoy a quiet evening in the old town.

meals.breakfast: At the hostel or grab something at Lagos train station before departing.
meals.lunch: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — a legendary local institution famous for its cataplana and fresh seafood. A must-visit. Budget ~€20–28 per person.
meals.dinner: A Forja in Lagos — a casual, authentic Portuguese restaurant popular with locals. Great grilled fish and meat dishes at honest prices. Budget ~€15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Trains from Lagos to Silves run several times daily — check the CP (Comboios de Portugal) schedule in advance. The walk from Silves train station to the castle is about 15 minutes uphill. Silves is also famous for its annual Medieval Fair (usually August) — September is quieter and more pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Dona Ana — one of the most beautiful and iconic beaches near Lagos, a short walk or taxi from the hostel. Arrive early to secure a good spot. The dramatic amber cliffs framing the beach make for spectacular scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the coastal cliff path from Praia de Dona Ana toward Praia do Camilo and Ponta da Piedade — a stunning 2–3 km clifftop walk with incredible views. Descend to Praia do Camilo for a final swim of the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a clifftop bar near Ponta da Piedade before heading back to Lagos for dinner.

meals.breakfast: At the hostel — fuel up before the beach and cliff walk day.
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia de Dona Ana — grilled fish, salad, and a cold drink. Budget ~€12–16.
meals.dinner: Casinha do Petisco in Lagos — a charming petiscos (Portuguese tapas) restaurant in the old town. Order several small plates to share — try the chouriço assado, gambas al ajillo, and local cheeses. Budget ~€18–24 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Praia de Dona Ana is about a 20-minute walk south from the hostel or a 5-minute taxi. The cliff walk to Ponta da Piedade is well-marked and relatively easy. Bring sunscreen, water, and a hat — the afternoon sun in September is still strong.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Portimão and Praia da Rocha. Catch a bus from Lagos (~20 minutes). Start with a visit to the Museu de Portimão — a fascinating free museum built inside a former sardine canning factory, telling the story of the region's fishing heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Rocha — a wide, golden urban beach backed by dramatic cliffs and a lively promenade. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing. The beach is larger and more animated than Lagos beaches, with a different energy.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Portimão's waterfront — the Largo 1º de Dezembro square is lined with restaurants and bars. Watch the fishing boats come in before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hostel before catching the bus.
meals.lunch: Taberna da Maré in Portimão — a waterfront restaurant famous for grilled sardines (sardinhas assadas), a quintessential Algarve experience. Budget ~€14–20.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Titanic in Portimão — a well-established mid-range restaurant with excellent seafood and regional wines. Budget ~€20–28 per person. Return to Lagos by bus after dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Buses between Lagos and Portimão run frequently throughout the day (Eva Transportes). The Museu de Portimão is free on Sunday afternoons. Praia da Rocha can be busy even in September — arrive by early afternoon for a good spot.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine-focused morning — visit a local wine shop in Lagos (Garrafeira do Mercado or similar) for a guided tasting of Algarve and wider Alentejo wines. Many shops offer informal tastings. Pick up regional wines, local honey, and artisan products as souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a final relaxed afternoon at Meia Praia — return to this beloved long beach for a leisurely swim and sunbathe. Hire a sunbed and umbrella (~€8–10) and enjoy the September sunshine with fewer crowds than peak summer.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Lagos' best restaurants — celebrate the trip with a special meal.

meals.breakfast: Café Central in Lagos old town — a classic Portuguese café with excellent coffee and fresh pastries. Budget ~€5–7.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach snack bar at Meia Praia — fresh salad, grilled fish, and a glass of local white wine. Budget ~€14–18.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Atlântico in Lagos — a highly regarded restaurant with panoramic sea views and a menu focused on the finest local seafood and Algarve wines. A special treat for the penultimate evening. Budget ~€30–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: September is an excellent time for wine shopping as the harvest (vindima) is underway — you may find newly released wines and special harvest events. Ask at the wine shop about any local harvest festivals or quinta open days happening during your visit.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning exploration — revisit your favourite spots in Lagos old town. Browse the Saturday market (Mercado Municipal de Lagos) if it's running — pick up fresh produce, local cheeses, smoked sausages, and handmade crafts as final souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last beach afternoon — head to Praia do Porto de Mós, a quieter and more natural beach west of Lagos, accessible by a 30-minute walk or short taxi. Enjoy a final swim in the Atlantic and soak up the last of the Algarve sunshine.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Lagos — take a slow walk through the old town, stop for a glass of wine at a favourite bar, and enjoy a relaxed last dinner.

meals.breakfast: At the hostel — enjoy a full breakfast to start the last full day.
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach — assemble a spread from the morning market: local bread, cheese, cured meats, olives, and fruit. Budget ~€10–12.
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Galeão in Lagos — a beloved local institution in the old town, known for generous portions of traditional Algarvian food and a warm atmosphere. Try the arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) or the grilled dourada. Budget ~€20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Praia do Porto de Mós is one of the least crowded beaches near Lagos and has a more natural, unspoiled feel. The walk there from the hostel takes about 30 minutes along a scenic coastal path — a lovely way to spend a final afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — pack up and check out of Boutique Taghostel. Take a last slow walk through Lagos, stop for a final coffee and pastel de nata at your favourite café, and say goodbye to the old town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Faro Airport — allow at least 2 hours before your flight. Take a taxi or pre-booked transfer from Lagos to Faro (~1 hour, ~€50–65 by taxi or ~€15–20 by shared shuttle). Check in and enjoy a final glass of Algarve wine at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and galão at a Lagos café — a perfect send-off. Budget ~€5–7.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Faro Airport or a café near the airport. Budget ~€10–15.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Check your return flight time carefully and plan your Lagos departure accordingly — the drive to Faro Airport takes approximately 60–75 minutes depending on traffic. Pre-book your airport transfer the night before to avoid any last-minute stress. Consider booking a shared shuttle service (e.g., Yellow Bus or GetTransfer) for a more economical option than a private taxi.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

experiences.name: Meia Praia Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxed afternoon at Meia Praia, one of the longest and most accessible beaches in the Algarve, located just minutes from Lagos town center. Ideal for a late Day 1 arrival — simply drop bags at a Lagos-based hotel and walk to the beach. Calm waters, golden sand, and beachside bars make it perfect for unwinding after a long flight without needing transport.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Cliff Walk and Swim
experiences.description: Explore the iconic golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear coves of Praia da Marinha, consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Stay in Carvoeiro or Lagoa to be within 10 minutes of this spot, avoiding long transfers. Morning visits offer calmer waters and fewer crowds, perfect for snorkeling and cliff photography.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine and Seafood Pairing Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided wine tasting session at a local quinta near Lagoa, the heart of Algarve wine country, sampling regional Negra Mole and Arinto wines paired with fresh local seafood and cheeses. Sessions typically run 2–3 hours and are hosted mid-morning, making them ideal for Day 2 or 3 when you are fully settled. Book a hotel in Lagoa or Silves to be within 15 minutes of multiple quintas.

experiences.name: Silves Castle and Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Discover the Moorish Silves Castle and wander the cobblestone streets of Portugal's former Algarve capital. Combine culture with food by joining a guided walking tour that stops at local taverns for regional wines, cataplana seafood stew, and medronho brandy. Silves is centrally located and easily reachable from Lagoa or Carvoeiro hotels in under 20 minutes, keeping transfers short and maximizing your day.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the famous Benagil Cave, one of the Algarve's most spectacular natural wonders, on a guided kayak tour departing directly from Benagil Beach. Tours last approximately 2 hours and depart in the morning when seas are calmest. Stay in Carvoeiro, just 5 km away, to avoid long travel and ensure you catch the early morning slot before afternoon winds pick up. A highlight activity well within budget.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. A pre-arranged private luxury transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar) whisks you to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos (~55 min). Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome glass of local Algarve wine left by the hotel.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight or airport
meals.dinner: Light late-night charcuterie and cheese board arranged by the hotel upon arrival, paired with a glass of Quinta dos Vales rosé

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your private airport transfer in advance. Confirm late check-in with Boutique Taghostel. Keep Day 1 light — rest is the priority after a long-haul flight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely gourmet breakfast at the hotel. Take a gentle orientation stroll through Lagos old town — explore the historic city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the charming cobblestone lanes to get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia Beach Day — one of the longest and most accessible beaches in the Algarve, just a short taxi or hotel shuttle ride from Lagos. Rent a premium sun lounger and parasol, swim in the calm Atlantic waters, and soak in the golden September sun. Arrange a beachside massage through the hotel concierge for the ultimate relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a sunset aperitivo on the rooftop or terrace of the hotel. Dine at Dom Sebastião restaurant in Lagos, a long-standing institution renowned for its grilled fish, cataplana seafood stew, and excellent regional wine list.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel — fresh pastries, local cheeses, smoked ham, fruit, and freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Meia Praia's upscale beach club — grilled sea bass, prawn skewers, and a chilled Alvarinho white wine
meals.dinner: Dom Sebastião Restaurant, Lagos — cataplana de marisco (seafood cataplana) paired with a bottle of Herdade do Esporão Reserva Branco

day_by_day.notes: September is ideal beach weather in the Algarve — warm, sunny, and less crowded than peak summer. Book Dom Sebastião in advance as it fills quickly.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, take a private guided boat tour departing from Lagos Marina. Cruise along the dramatic Ponta da Piedade coastline — weave through golden sea arches, hidden grottos, and sea stacks unique to the western Algarve. A private charter ensures exclusivity and flexibility.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east along the coast to Praia da Marinha Cliff Walk and Swim. Explore the iconic golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear coves consistently ranked among Europe's most beautiful beaches. Take the cliff-top trail for panoramic views, then descend to swim in the turquoise waters.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to the charming village of Carvoeiro for sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar. Dine at Bon Bon Restaurant (Michelin-starred) in Carvoeiro for an extraordinary tasting menu showcasing modern Portuguese cuisine with Algarve ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, artisan breads, and local honey
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch box prepared by the hotel, enjoyed on the cliffs at Praia da Marinha — charcuterie, local cheeses, olives, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Bon Bon Restaurant, Carvoeiro — 7-course tasting menu with wine pairing featuring local Algarve and Alentejo wines

day_by_day.notes: Book Bon Bon Restaurant well in advance — it is Michelin-starred and highly sought after. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Praia da Marinha cliff trail. Bring reef shoes for rocky cove entry.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Lagos after breakfast for the Algarve Wine and Seafood Pairing Experience near Lagoa (~30 min drive). Join a guided wine tasting session at a local quinta in the heart of Algarve wine country. Explore the vineyards, learn about the region's unique Negra Mole and Arinto grape varieties, and taste a curated selection of whites, reds, and the famous Algarve medronho brandy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the experience with a guided seafood and wine pairing lunch at the quinta. Afterwards, explore the charming town of Lagoa and visit the local market for artisan products, ceramics, and local preserves to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a relaxed evening with a sunset walk along the Lagos seafront promenade. Dine at A Forja restaurant in Lagos — a beloved local gem known for its perfectly grilled fish and traditional Portuguese recipes.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread with fresh fruit platters, yogurt, granola, and pastéis de nata
meals.lunch: Included in the Algarve Wine and Seafood Pairing Experience at the quinta — grilled octopus, clams, and regional cheeses paired with estate wines
meals.dinner: A Forja Restaurant, Lagos — grilled whole sea bream with roasted vegetables and a bottle of Quinta do Crasto white

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the wine and seafood pairing experience as group sizes are limited. Designate a driver or arrange a private transfer for the wine tasting day to enjoy the pairings fully.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and use the hotel's amenities. Optional: book a private yoga session on the hotel terrace or a spa treatment if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lagos in depth — visit the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos), the Igreja de Santo António with its stunning gilded baroque interior, and browse the boutique shops along Rua Cândido dos Reis for local crafts, ceramics, and fashion.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at Stevie Ray's Jazz Bar in Lagos — a sophisticated spot with live jazz and expertly crafted cocktails. Dinner at Casinha do Petisco, a refined petisco (Portuguese tapas) restaurant offering creative small plates and an impressive natural wine list.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast — freshly baked croissants, smoked salmon, avocado, local jams, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at Restaurante O Camilo, perched dramatically above Praia do Camilo — fresh grilled fish and salads with stunning cliff views
meals.dinner: Casinha do Petisco, Lagos — tasting selection of petiscos: bacalhau à brás croquettes, razor clams, black pork secretos, paired with natural Alentejo wines

day_by_day.notes: Saturday evenings in Lagos can be lively — the old town comes alive with locals and visitors. Book dinner reservations in advance for weekend evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure for the Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour (~1 hour drive east to Lagoa/Benagil). Paddle through the world-famous Benagil Cave — one of the Algarve's most spectacular natural wonders — on a private guided kayak tour. The private tour ensures you arrive before the crowds and have the cave largely to yourselves.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax on the small beach inside Benagil Cave or on nearby Praia de Benagil. Explore the surrounding coastline by kayak, discovering hidden sea caves and arches inaccessible by foot.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Lagos via Portimão. Stop for a sunset drink at a clifftop bar in Alvor. Dinner at Tasca da Dona Barca in Portimão — a celebrated traditional restaurant famous for its sardines, grilled fish, and authentic Algarvian recipes.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel — yogurt, fruit, and espresso before the tour
meals.lunch: Post-kayak lunch at Restaurante O Litoral in Carvoeiro — fresh catch of the day, grilled prawns, and a crisp Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Tasca da Dona Barca, Portimão — grilled sardines, amêijoas à Bulhão Pato (clams), and regional desserts with a bottle of Quinta dos Vales Grande Reserva

day_by_day.notes: Book the private Benagil kayak tour well in advance — it is one of the most popular experiences in the Algarve. Bring water shoes, sunscreen, and a waterproof bag for valuables. The cave is best visited in the morning for optimal light.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — depart Lagos after breakfast (~30 min drive). Begin with the Silves Castle and Old Town Food Walk. Explore the magnificent red sandstone Moorish castle, one of the best-preserved in Portugal, with panoramic views over the Algarve interior. A private guide brings the history to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the food walk through Silves' cobblestone streets — taste local specialties including carob products, fig and almond sweets, smoked sausages, and artisan cheeses at family-run shops. Visit the Gothic Silves Cathedral and the Municipal Museum of Archaeology.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a quiet evening — perhaps a private sunset sailing trip from Lagos Marina (arrange through the hotel concierge). Dinner at Vasco da Gama restaurant in Lagos for a refined take on traditional Portuguese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread with local specialties
meals.lunch: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — a legendary seafood institution; try the cataplana and grilled tiger prawns with local Algarve wine
meals.dinner: Vasco da Gama, Lagos — slow-roasted suckling pig, black pork tenderloin, and a bottle of Herdade do Mouchão Tonel red

day_by_day.notes: Silves is particularly beautiful in September when the summer crowds have thinned. The Silves Medieval Fair (usually August) may have just ended, leaving the town in a relaxed, authentic state. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestone walking.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated beach morning at Praia do Camilo — one of Lagos' most dramatic and beautiful small beaches, a short walk from the hotel. Arrive early to secure the best spot. Swim in the crystal-clear waters framed by towering golden cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a leisurely lunch and afternoon spa treatment or pool time. Alternatively, take a private stand-up paddleboard lesson arranged through the hotel concierge at Meia Praia.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo at the hotel terrace. Dine at No Pátio restaurant in Lagos — a romantic courtyard restaurant with an intimate atmosphere, excellent wine cellar, and creative Portuguese-Mediterranean menu.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs any style, fresh pastries, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel or at Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — fresh grilled fish, salads, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: No Pátio, Lagos — duck rice, grilled turbot, and a curated wine pairing with Douro and Alentejo selections

day_by_day.notes: Praia do Camilo requires a descent via wooden stairs — arrive early as the small beach fills up even in September. The afternoon is a perfect opportunity to rest mid-trip.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwestern tip of continental Europe (~45 min drive from Lagos). Visit the dramatic Sagres Fortress perched on the clifftops, explore the wind-swept promontory, and stand at Cabo de São Vicente lighthouse for breathtaking Atlantic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sagres village — visit the local fish market, browse surf shops, and relax at Praia do Martinhal, a sheltered and beautiful beach near Sagres ideal for swimming and paddleboarding.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos via the scenic coastal road. Sunset drinks at the rooftop of a Lagos hotel bar. Dinner at Restaurante Adega da Marina — a Lagos institution with a vast wine cellar, live fado music on select evenings, and exceptional grilled seafood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread
meals.lunch: A Sagres — fresh tuna steak, grilled barnacles (percebes), and local bread at a seafront restaurant in Sagres village
meals.dinner: Adega da Marina, Lagos — grilled lobster, mixed seafood rice, and a bottle of Niepoort Redoma Branco, with possible live fado accompaniment

day_by_day.notes: Cabo de São Vicente can be very windy — bring a light jacket even in September. The drive along the Costa Vicentina is stunningly scenic. Check if Adega da Marina has fado scheduled for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Second visit to the Algarve Wine Country — this time explore a different quinta near Monchique or Tavira for a contrasting wine experience. Arrange a private vineyard tour and barrel tasting, focusing on the region's red wines and late-harvest dessert wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive up to Monchique — the lush mountain village in the Serra de Monchique (~45 min from Lagos). Explore the charming village, visit the ruins of the Franciscan convent, and enjoy the cooler mountain air and panoramic views over the Algarve coast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Relaxed evening with a private in-room dinner arranged by the hotel — a curated chef's menu delivered to your suite with a premium wine selection, for an intimate and exclusive experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — extended leisurely spread
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Central in Monchique — traditional mountain cuisine featuring smoked chouriço, roast kid (cabrito), and medronho brandy
meals.dinner: Private in-room chef's dinner at Boutique Taghostel — 4-course menu with local ingredients: amuse-bouche, seafood starter, meat main, and almond tart dessert, paired with a curated wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the private in-room dinner experience at least 48 hours in advance with the hotel concierge. Monchique is a refreshing contrast to the coastal heat — the mountain air is noticeably cooler and the scenery dramatically different.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning at Meia Praia — return to this expansive beach for a final long beach morning. Rent a kayak or take a paddleboard lesson, swim, and simply relax. The beach is calmer on weekday mornings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for a premium shopping afternoon — visit artisan ceramic studios, local wine shops (stock up on Algarve wines to take home), and boutique fashion stores along the old town streets. Visit the Lagos Municipal Market for local produce, honey, and preserves.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner cocktails at a rooftop bar in Lagos with views over the old town and marina. Final gala dinner at Bon Bon Restaurant (if not visited earlier) or return to a favourite restaurant from the trip for a memorable last evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread with a celebratory touch: sparkling wine and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Meia Praia beach club — grilled fish of the day, salads, and a final glass of chilled Alvarinho
meals.dinner: Gala farewell dinner — Bon Bon Restaurant, Carvoeiro (Michelin-starred) or Dom Sebastião, Lagos — full tasting menu with premium wine pairing to celebrate the trip

day_by_day.notes: Use the afternoon shopping session to purchase wine, ceramics, and local products as gifts or souvenirs. Pack wines carefully with wine travel bags available at local shops. Book the farewell dinner well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning in Lagos — enjoy a long, unhurried breakfast at the hotel. Take a last stroll through the old town, visit the waterfront, and say goodbye to the Lagos Marina and Ponta da Piedade viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, enjoy a final swim at Praia da Batata (the closest beach to the hotel, just minutes away) or relax at the hotel. Begin packing and preparing for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Casual farewell dinner in Lagos old town — choose a relaxed wine bar or petisco spot for a low-key final evening. Retire early if departing the following morning.

meals.breakfast: Extended final hotel breakfast — order everything you loved during the stay
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at Restaurante O Camilo — final grilled fish with a view of the cliffs
meals.dinner: Wine bar dinner at Casinha do Petisco or a relaxed meal at Restaurante Adega da Marina — light petiscos, local wine, and a final medronho digestif

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the hotel. Arrange luggage storage if needed for a late departure. Tip hotel staff generously for exceptional service throughout the stay.

day_by_day.morning: Final breakfast at the hotel. Check out and arrange private luxury transfer to Faro Airport (~55 min). Depart the Algarve with extraordinary memories of beaches, wine, food, and the golden light of southern Portugal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Faro Airport. Arrive with ample time — allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or at destination.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a quick espresso and pastel de nata at a café near the hotel before transfer
meals.lunch: Airport lunch at Faro Airport or in-flight
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the private return airport transfer. Confirm all wine and fragile purchases are properly packed in checked luggage. Keep a small carry-on bag with essentials for the journey home. Consider joining the TAP Miles & Go or relevant frequent flyer program to earn points on your return flight.
